definition: Aberration means something that differs from the norm, a single irregular departure from what is expected.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word aberration. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know aberration should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Coach Rivera told reporters that the team's sloppy first half was an aberration, one off night in an otherwise disciplined season.
A hiccup is a tiny interruption that everyone forgets by tomorrow, while an aberration is a genuine departure from a well-established pattern.
An aberration is a single irregular exception, but a monstrosity is a departure so extreme that it shocks everyone who encounters it.

An irregularity is something that fails to follow the usual rule or pattern, and unlike an aberration it can happen again and again. An aberration is a single break in an otherwise steady record; once the same flaw keeps returning, irregularity is the honest word for it.

A fluke is a one-time stroke of chance, usually a lucky result that cannot be planned or repeated. An aberration is also a one-off, but it simply breaks an established pattern, lucky or not, and it more often points at something going wrong than at a happy accident.

An oddity is a thing that is strange in itself, wherever it turns up. An aberration is strange only against the record around it: a perfectly ordinary event can still be an aberration if it breaks an otherwise steady, well-established pattern.

In eleven years of running the Lighthouse Cafe, Dot had never once burned the morning cinnamon rolls.
The charred batch she pulled from the oven that Friday was such an aberration that the regulars joked the smoke alarm had never even been tested before.
One burned batch in eleven flawless years is a single, temporary departure from the cafe's normal record, which is exactly what an aberration is.
Aberration names a single, temporary departure from an established pattern, so it works best when the surrounding record is steady: one bad game, one strange reading, one uncharacteristic outburst.
If the irregularities keep happening, they are no longer aberrations but the new pattern.

For thirty-one years, the Route 9 bus driven by Mr.
Okafor had pulled into the depot within a minute of schedule.
Riders set their watches by him; the depot manager joked that the clocks were checked against the bus, not the bus against the clocks.
So the Tuesday the bus rolled in nineteen minutes late, the whole depot fell quiet.
The lateness was an aberration, and everyone sensed it: not a habit forming, just one crack in a record too steady to doubt.
A fallen oak across the county road explained everything, and by Wednesday the bus was back within its minute, the streak effectively unbroken.
